recipes.name: Code-native GUI environment reconstruction
recipes.summary: Rebuild a real application as a lightweight self-contained web environment and make the reward code-native: executable assertions over DOM and application state instead of noisy visual proxies.
recipes.background: Reconstruct a real application as a lightweight, fast, self-contained web environment with a code model, then make the reward code-native: executable assertions over DOM and application state instead of noisy visual proxies. One unified specification plus task-centric test-driven development keeps multi-page applications coherent.
needs: can serve a local web app
recipes.produces: A self-contained web environment plus a task whose reward is an executable assertion over DOM text, element state or application state.
when_to_use: the source is a web or desktop application, or a screenshot of one
training on the real application is too slow, too costly or not reproducible
you need many trials, so environment latency dominates the budget
not_when_to_use: the task depends on the real backend, real user data or real network calls
the visual fidelity of the original application is itself the graded property
inputs: the target application or a reference design image
a code model able to emit a working front-end
a seed describing the site or app to keep reconstructions diverse

steps.title: Pick the application and the scope
steps.detail: Choose which screens, flows and data actually matter for the task; a faithful clone of everything is neither cheap nor necessary.
steps.accept: The screens, flows and data the task needs are listed, and the rest of the application is out of scope.

steps.title: Reconstruct as a lightweight web environment
steps.detail: Have a multimodal code model rebuild the application as a small self-contained web environment, with local seed data and no external calls.
steps.accept: The environment serves the scoped flows from local seed data and makes no external calls.

steps.title: Write one unified specification
steps.detail: Specify routes, pages, shared components and the data model once, so every generated page belongs to the same application.
steps.accept: Routes, pages, shared components and the data model are specified once, and every generated page conforms to them.

steps.title: Develop task-centric, test first
steps.detail: Build the smallest environment that supports the task, with the test written before the page; task-centric test-driven development is what stops multi-page apps from drifting.
steps.accept: The test for the task exists and fails before the page that satisfies it is written.

steps.title: Attach code-native rewards
steps.detail: Express the reward as executable assertions over DOM text, element state or application state; a visual estimate of success is too noisy to train on.
steps.accept: The reward is an executable assertion over DOM text, element state or application state.

steps.title: Generate the task evaluators
steps.detail: Derive a verifiable evaluator per task so the reward can be dense during training rather than only at the end.
steps.accept: Each task has an evaluator that fails on the pristine environment and can be applied during the episode, not only at the end.

curation_notes: Vary the reconstructions with a website seed plus a reference design image, otherwise every environment converges on the same look and the same flows.
verifier: executable assertions over the DOM or application state
an evaluator that fails on the pristine environment
environment latency low enough to run many trials per epoch
pitfalls: visual proxies for success are noisy and reward formatting instead of behaviour
multi-page coherence breaks unless one specification drives every page
a reconstruction that silently needs the network is not reproducible

source_papers.title: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
source_papers.note: reconstructs real applications into lightweight web environments with code-native executable rewards

source_papers.title: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
source_papers.note: unified specification, task-centric test-driven development, seed plus reference design image for diversity, generated evaluators

recipes.name: Explore-first reverse task synthesis for web agents
recipes.summary: Act first, write the task afterwards: sweep the site into a map of page states and transitions, propose tasks from the map, execute them, and repair instruction and trajectory until a trajectory scorer accepts the pair.
recipes.background: Invert the usual order: the agent acts in the environment first and the task is written afterwards from what it saw. Exploration is a structured sweep, not free-form scrolling, and it produces a map of the site's functionally distinct page states and the executable interactions that move between them, so rare branches are covered instead of over-sampled popular ones. Candidate tasks are proposed from that map, executed in the environment, and jointly repaired with their trajectories whenever the instruction and the execution disagree; a trajectory-level reward model rejects pairs whose wording is not grounded in what was actually performed. The map also supplies the graph structure used to compose multi-step tasks without cycles.
recipes.produces: A web task with a recorded trajectory that reaches its goal state, plus the site map of states and transitions it was derived from.
when_to_use: the source is a live or captured site whose task surface is not known in advance
many diverse tasks are needed and manual authoring does not scale
tasks must be grounded in behaviours the site actually exposes
not_when_to_use: the site's functionality is fully known and small, so a direct task list is cheaper
the environment has destructive or irreversible side effects that exploration must not trigger
inputs: an executable environment for the site, live or replayed
an explorer agent that can act and observe
a proposal model that turns observed states into candidate instructions

steps.title: Explore with a structured sweep
steps.detail: Move through the site by its own navigation affordances, recording each distinct page state and the interaction that produced it. Uniform random clicking over-samples common flows and misses the rare transitions that make tasks worth training on.
steps.accept: Each functionally distinct page state is recorded together with the interaction that produced it.

steps.title: Assemble the website map
steps.detail: Organise the observations into a map of functionally distinct page states and the transitions between them, with the elements that trigger each transition. The map is the artifact the tasks are derived from and the ground for any coverage claim.
steps.accept: The map lists the distinct page states and, for each transition, the element that triggers it.

steps.title: Propose tasks from the map
steps.detail: Derive candidate instructions from the observed states and transitions, so the task language is anchored in what the site supports rather than in what the model imagines a website of that kind should contain.
steps.accept: Each candidate instruction names a state or a transition that the map actually contains.

steps.title: Execute and record
steps.detail: Run each candidate in the environment and keep the trajectory that reached the goal together with the states visited, so the instruction can later be checked against the execution rather than trusted.
steps.accept: The candidate ran to its stated goal state and both its trajectory and its visited states are stored.

steps.title: Co-repair instruction and trajectory
steps.detail: When instruction and trajectory disagree, edit both: fix the wording where the trajectory is right, and regenerate the trajectory where the instruction states a behaviour the site does support. Accepting the mismatch leaves supervision that teaches the agent to describe something other than what it did.
steps.accept: After the repair the stored trajectory and the instruction describe the same behaviour.

steps.title: Filter for alignment
steps.detail: Score the pairs with a trajectory-level reward model that checks the instruction against the executed trajectory, and drop the pairs whose wording cannot be grounded in the performance.
steps.accept: A trajectory-level reward model scored each pair, and the pairs whose wording is not grounded in the execution were dropped.

steps.title: Compose along the transition graph
steps.detail: Extend verified tasks along the map's graph by planning paths that do not revisit a state, so multi-step tasks grow long without turning into cyclic loops.
steps.accept: The composed path revisits no state.

curation_notes: Retain the map and the set of states covered by the retained tasks, so later rounds can target the states and transitions that are still unrepresented.
verifier: each retained instruction is graded against its own recorded trajectory, and pairs whose trajectory does not support the instruction are rejected
every state in a composed task's path is distinct, so the path contains no cycle
each candidate task was executed in the environment and reached its stated goal state at least once
the recorded trajectory replays in the environment and produces the same final state
pitfalls: tasks proposed before exploration describe a website that does not exist and are unexecutable by construction
unfiltered exploration over-samples the landing page and yields many near-duplicate tasks
repairing only the instruction, or only the trajectory, leaves the pair misaligned
a trajectory collected on a live site stops replaying once the site changes

source_papers.title: OS-Genesis: Automating GUI Agent Trajectory Construction via Reverse Task Synthesis
source_papers.note: agents perceive the environment and interact step by step first, then the task is derived retrospectively from the trajectory, with a trajectory reward model enforcing quality

source_papers.title: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
source_papers.note: structured exploration producing a website map of functionally distinct page states and executable interactions, page-level and transition-level supervision, and joint repair of inconsistent task-trajectory pairs

source_papers.title: SEE: Structure-aware Exploring & Exploiting for Long-horizon GUI Agent Trajectory Synthesis
source_papers.note: explicit UI transition graph over screens and elements, then graph-based synthesis that plans multi-step trajectories and controls sampling to prevent spurious cycles

recipes.name: HTTP capture and replay replica with repair loop
recipes.summary: Capture the real site at the HTTP layer and replay it from a local server: explore to complete the capture, verify and repair it, then write tasks over the navigation skills the capture confirmed.
recipes.background: The fidelity of a synthetic web environment comes from the real site rather than from a code model, so the site is captured at the HTTP layer and replayed. A browser session records the response bodies, headers and redirects for every URL it reaches, and a local server serves those recordings, so pages look and behave like the original while the environment stays deterministic, resettable and cheap to run per rollout. The capture is not a blind dump: an explorer drives the site to discover its reachable URLs and interaction outcomes, and an independent verifier checks the frozen candidate and directs repairs, either fixing the local replay or recapturing only the URLs that cannot be fixed. Tasks are then written over the navigation skills the exploration actually confirmed, which keeps them inside the behaviour the replica supports.
recipes.produces: A local replica serving the recorded bytes at the original paths, plus a task whose success is a comparison over replica state or recorded artifacts.
when_to_use: the source is a real website whose visual fidelity and content matter
the live site is unstable, login-gated or too slow to afford per rollout
thousands of rollouts are needed, so per-episode setup cost must approach zero
not_when_to_use: the task depends on live backend state changing in response to the agent, which a replay cannot reproduce
the source is a desktop or mobile application rather than a web page
inputs: a browser session, authenticated if needed, against the source site
a recording layer that captures responses at the HTTP layer
a local server that replays the recording plus a repair loop that can recapture URLs

steps.title: Scope the site to a bounded surface
steps.detail: Decide which pages, entry points and authenticated areas the tasks will use. A capture of an entire site is unbounded, and the replay drifts as the site's reachable surface grows.
steps.accept: The pages, entry points and authenticated areas in scope are listed, and everything else is left out of the capture.

steps.title: Record at the HTTP layer
steps.detail: Drive a browser session through the scoped surface and store the response body, status, headers and redirect target under each request key. Cache assets instead of re-fetching them so a rollout costs no network time.
steps.accept: Each scoped request key has a stored body, status, headers and redirect target, and assets are cached rather than re-fetched.

steps.title: Replay locally behind the same URLs
steps.detail: Serve the recording from a local origin that mirrors the original path structure, so links, forms and redirects behave as they did and the agent sees the real page rather than a mock-up of it.
steps.accept: The local server serves the recorded bytes at the original paths, and the links, forms and redirects behave as recorded.

steps.title: Explore to complete the capture
steps.detail: Run an explorer over the replica to discover the URLs the pages actually link to and the interactions that work. Any URL reached but not recorded is either recaptured or explicitly marked unavailable, so the replay never serves an empty body for a real link.
steps.accept: Every URL reached during exploration is either recorded or explicitly marked unavailable, and none returns an empty body.

steps.title: Verify and repair the frozen candidate
steps.detail: Have an independent checker confirm the captured pages against the source for structural and content fidelity and point at the mismatches; repair locally where possible and recapture only the URLs that cannot be fixed, so the loop terminates.
steps.accept: An independent checker compared the captured pages with the source, and each mismatch is either repaired locally or recaptured.

steps.title: Ground tasks in observed navigation
steps.detail: Write tasks from the navigation skills exploration confirmed, such as filtering, paging, form entry and cross-page linking, so each task is one the replica can actually support.
steps.accept: The task uses a navigation skill that exploration confirmed works on the replica.

steps.title: Attach deterministic checks
steps.detail: Express each task's success against the replica's recorded artifacts and backend state, so the reward is a comparison over bytes and rows rather than a visual estimate.
steps.accept: Success is a comparison over replica state or recorded artifacts and needs no visual or model judgement.

curation_notes: Store the recording and its checksums with the task set, because a capture that drifts silently makes earlier scores incomparable.
Recapture the URLs whose content changes on the live site before comparing runs, since such content can only be verified from the snapshot it was captured in.
verifier: every URL referenced by a task returns the recorded response in the replay, with matching status and content checksum
the local replay returns identical bytes for a recorded URL across repeated requests
a task's success check is a comparison over replica state or recorded artifacts, not a visual or model judgement
the environment resets to the recorded initial state by checksum equality
pitfalls: capturing pages without capturing their transitions yields a replica in which the task cannot be completed
a replay that silently serves an empty body for an uncached link looks broken to the agent and to the check
letting the verifier and the capturer share the same code path hides systematic capture errors
content that changes on the live site makes the capture a snapshot, and tasks depending on that part cannot be verified from it

source_papers.title: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
source_papers.note: HTTP-level caching that captures and replays stable visual states while preserving interactive behaviour, combined with LLM-based environment synthesis grounded in real websites and core web navigation skills

source_papers.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
source_papers.note: Explorer-Builder collects browser-observable structures, resources and interaction outcomes from real URLs, and an independent verifier checks frozen candidates and directs local repair or targeted source recapture

source_papers.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
source_papers.note: task-driven reconstruction that keeps visual interfaces, content and functional workflows faithful, with audits of visual fidelity, functional correctness and task validity
